RydAR/Data and privacy

Data and privacy

Know what your drive shares.

The iPhone app can check the road surface and optionally share anonymous curve passes. Here is how those features work in the current implementation.

Camera frames stay on the phone

When the road-surface check runs in Driver mode, the drive screen shows a small live preview and a Paved or Unpaved label. Frames are displayed and processed on the phone; they are not saved or uploaded. Teen driver mode does not use the camera.

Anonymous curve sharing is optional

When uploads are enabled, anonymous curve passes are held until the trip ends, then sent together in random order. They are sent only if uploads are still enabled when the trip ends. Simulator builds do not upload passes.

A pass includes a curve identifier, travel direction, speed value, hour bucket, and app version. The server stores the day of arrival rather than its exact time. Curve and time information can still be sensitive; turn off sharing if you do not want to contribute passes.

The public county CSV exports contain aggregated counts per curve and the number of distinct hour buckets, not individual trip records. Read the API implementation for the fields stored and exported.

Location and the web map

Your browser may ask for location access to position the Arkansas curve map near you. You can decline and choose a county manually. RydAR’s map code uses that location locally to position the view; it does not post it to the anonymous-pass API.

The map loads basemap styles and tiles from OpenFreeMap. Those requests, as well as requests to the RydAR hosting provider, expose ordinary connection information such as an IP address. Apple’s TestFlight and GitHub have their own privacy terms when you follow their links.

Questions about the implementation

RydAR’s source code is public. You can open an issue with a question or bug report. Avoid including personal trip details in a public issue.
